source.title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology

accepted.question_text: Let X be a Lindelöf topological space, meaning every open cover of X has a countable subcover. Assume also that every point x in X is a Gδ-point, i.e. the singleton {x} is a countable intersection of open sets in X. Must the cardinality of X satisfy |X| ≤ 2^ω?

evidence.quote: Problem 1 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1969). Suppose that X is a Lindelöf space such that every point of X is a Gδ-point. Then is it true that |X| ≤ 2^ω?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a compact topological space X together with a family {η_x : x ∈ X}, where each η_x is a decreasing sequence (V_n(x): n ∈ ω) of subsets containing x and such that a set U is open exactly when for every x ∈ U there is n with V_n(x) ⊂ U, for which X is weakly first-countable in this sense and has cardinality |X| > 2^ω?

evidence.quote: Problem 2 (Arhangel’skii, 1966). Give an example in ZF C of a weakly first-countable compact space X such that |X| > 2^ω.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist, in ZFC, a compact topological space X that is weakly first-countable—meaning X carries a family of decreasing sequences of neighborhoods in the sense defined in the paper, sufficient to determine the open sets—but is nevertheless not first-countable?
accepted.context_brief: Weakly first-countable but not first-countable compacta

evidence.quote: Problem 3 (Arhangel’skii, < 1978). Give an example in ZF C of a weakly first-countable, but not first-countable, compact space X.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a weakly first-countable topological space, in the sense that openness is determined by pointwise decreasing sequences of sets as in the paper. Assume in addition that the Souslin number of X is countable, meaning every family of pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets of X is countable. Must |X| ≤ 2^ω hold?
accepted.context_brief: Weakly first-countable spaces with countable Souslin number

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Arhangel’skii, < 1980). Suppose that X is a weakly first-countable space such that the Souslin number of X is countable. Then is it true that |X| ≤ 2^ω?

accepted.question_text: If X is a symmetrizable space, meaning its topology is generated by some symmetric d on X with d(x,y)=0 exactly when x=y and d(x,y)=d(y,x), must every point of X be a Gδ-point?

evidence.quote: Problem 5 (< 1970). Is every point in a symmetrizable space a Gδ?

accepted.question_text: If X is a pseudocompact symmetrizable space, where symmetrizability is understood via a topology generated by a symmetric and pseudocompactness means every continuous real-valued function on X is bounded, must X be first-countable?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Is every pseudocompact symmetrizable space first-countable?

accepted.question_text: Is every pseudocompact symmetrizable space necessarily a Moore space?
accepted.context_brief: Pseudocompact symmetrizable spaces as Moore spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Is every pseudocompact symmetrizable space a Moore space?

accepted.question_text: Construct, in ZFC, a countable topological group that is Fréchet-Urysohn—so whenever a point lies in the closure of a set, some sequence from that set converges to the point—but is not metrizable.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 (V. I. Malykhin, < 1980). Construct in ZF C a non-metrizable countable Fréchet-Urysohn topological group.

accepted.question_text: Construct, in ZFC, a non-discrete topological group whose underlying space is extremally disconnected, meaning that the closure of every open subset is open.

evidence.quote: Problem 9 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1967). Construct in ZF C a non-discrete extremally disconnected topological group.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a paracompact p-space, that is, a space that arises as the preimage of a metrizable space under a perfect mapping. Is the free topological group F(X) on X necessarily paracompact?
accepted.context_brief: Free topological groups on paracompact p-spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 10 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, 1981). Is the free topological group F(X) of an arbitrary paracompact p-space X paracompact?

accepted.question_text: Construct, in ZFC, countably compact topological groups G and H such that the product group G × H fails to be countably compact.

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Construct in ZF C countably compact topological groups G and H such that their product G × H is not countably compact.

accepted.question_text: Construct, in ZFC, a countably compact topological group G such that its square G × G is not countably compact.
accepted.context_brief: Square of a countably compact group

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Construct in ZF C a countably compact topological group G such that its square G × G is not countably compact.

accepted.question_text: Does every infinite homogeneous compact space contain a non-trivial convergent sequence? Here homogeneous means that for any two points x and y there is a homeomorphism of the space sending x to y.

evidence.quote: Problem 13 (W. Rudin, 1956). Is it true that every infinite homogeneous compact space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary compact space Y, does there always exist a homogeneous compact space X and a continuous surjection from X onto Y?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact space Y as an image of a homogeneous compact space X under a continuous mapping?

accepted.question_text: If X is a homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space, meaning that the closure of every countable subset of X is metrizable, must X be first-countable?

evidence.quote: Problem 15 (Arhangel’skii, 1987). Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space X first-countable?

accepted.question_text: If X is a homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space, where the closure of every countable subset of X is metrizable, must the cardinality of X satisfy |X| ≤ 2^ω?

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact space X not greater than 2^ω?

accepted.question_text: Does every nonempty monolithic compact space have at least one point at which the space is first-countable?
accepted.context_brief: Monolithic compacta and local first countability

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Is it true that every nonempty monolithic compact space is first-countable at some point?

accepted.question_text: Let Cp(X) denote the space of real-valued continuous functions on a space X with the topology of pointwise convergence. Two spaces X and Y are called t-equivalent when Cp(X) and Cp(Y) are homeomorphic. Is the closed unit interval I t-equivalent to the square I^2?

evidence.quote: Problem 18 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, ≤ 1989). Is the unit segment I t-equivalent to the square I^2?

accepted.question_text: Let t-equivalence mean homeomorphism between the function spaces Cp(X) and Cp(Y), where Cp(X) is the space of real-valued continuous functions on X with the topology of pointwise convergence. Is the closed unit interval I t-equivalent to the Cantor set?
accepted.context_brief: t-equivalence of the interval and Cantor set

evidence.quote: Problem 19 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, ≤ 1989). Is the unit segment I t-equivalent to the Cantor set?

accepted.question_text: If two spaces X and Y are t-equivalent, meaning their pointwise-convergence function spaces Cp(X) and Cp(Y) are homeomorphic, is topological dimension dim preserved by this equivalence, at least for separable metrizable spaces or for compact spaces?

evidence.quote: Problem 20 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, ≤ 1985). Is the dimension dim preserved by the t-equivalence, at least in the class of separable metrizable spaces or in the class of compacta?
